brief: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky frames the current setup as a positioning paradox: bond vol has retraced roughly 30% of its recent spike and Treasury auctions were well absorbed, so if yields stabilize the drag on growth eases, and speculators are heavily short bonds and Russell while long Nasdaq, so calming bonds becomes a squeeze in the under-owned names, not a crash. US hedge fund net leverage sits near 2-year lows (46.9%, 2nd percentile) even as the S&P hovers near record highs, while gross leverage is at an 80th-percentile high, meaning plenty of exposure but almost no net conviction. Within that, hedge funds rotated out of Info Tech last week after one OpenAI revenue headline triggered forced selling, read as evidence the AI long is the market's most crowded, nervous position. The same under-ownership argument extends to Europe: a new EU/China hybrid-auto deal, calmer French bond spreads and CTAs holding only ~$10bn of European equity length versus ~$40bn in the US leave room for a catch-up trade. The piece caveats that the energy shock (Brent ~$103) is unresolved and that Wednesday's CPI print is the key risk to the whole thesis.
